title: Web UI dead in real browsers: ApiClient calls unbound global fetch → Illegal invocation
description:
LIVE BUG (found testing launched app). Overview shows dead/NO SIGNAL state; every /api/* call fails with 'cannot reach the local server' (AppError kind=network) in a real browser, while curl + all vitest tests pass.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via CDP against the running server): web/src/api/client.ts:137 stores the global fetch UNBOUND — 'this.#fetch = opts.fetchImpl ?? fetch' — and invokes it as 'this.#fetch(url, init)'. In Chrome/Safari/Firefox, window.fetch is this-sensitive: calling it with this=ApiClient instance throws TypeError: Failed to execute 'fetch' on 'Window': Illegal invocation, BEFORE any request is issued (CDP shows zero Network.requestWillBeSent for /api/*). The #get/#send catch maps the TypeError to ApiError(0,'network') → shell renders SIGNAL LOST 'cannot reach the local server'. Node's undici fetch ignores this, so the full test suite and CLI report path never see it.

REPRO: npm run build; node dist/cli/index.js launch --no-open; open the printed URL in Chrome → SIGNAL LOST; devtools console shows Illegal invocation. curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <tok>' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/report returns 2 agents.

FIX: bind at storage — this.#fetch = opts.fetchImpl ?? fetch.bind(globalThis) (or wrap in an arrow). ONE site; ws/client.ts uses 'new WebSocket' (constructor, not this-sensitive) — clean.

REGRESSION TEST: in client.test, stub a this-sensitive fetch (function that throws unless this===globalThis||this===undefined after bind semantics) as the GLOBAL and construct ApiClient WITHOUT fetchImpl; assert a #get succeeds. Must fail on the unbound form.

VERIFY: rebuild, relaunch, drive real Chrome (headless CDP) → Overview renders CLAUDE-CODE + CODEX SignalStrips, stats agents=2.
acceptance_criteria: ApiClient default fetch is bound/wrapped; unit regression test that fails on unbound form; headless Chrome against launched server renders 2 agent SignalStrips on Overview; tsc/eslint/prettier/vitest green
notes: Fixed unbound browser fetch: web/src/api/client.ts constructor now uses opts.fetchImpl ?? fetch.bind(globalThis) (injected fetchImpl unchanged, comment added). Regression test added in web/src/api/client.test.ts: 'ApiClient default fetch binding > calls the global fetch with globalThis as `this` (browser fetch is this-sensitive)' using vi.stubGlobal + vi.unstubAllGlobals; verified it FAILS (ApiError status 0 network, 'Illegal invocation') on the unbound form and passes with the fix. Gates (direct binaries): tsc --noEmit clean; eslint client.ts+client.test.ts clean; prettier --check src/** web/src/** clean; vitest run web/src/api = 2 files / 32 tests passed. Not committed (orchestrator commits).
close_reason: Fixed in b0b1782: default fetch bound to globalThis (client.ts); regression test fails on unbound form; adversarial review APPROVE (bug-class sweep of web/src found no other this-sensitive stored globals); verified live in headless Chrome via CDP — Overview renders 2 AGENTS (CLAUDE-CODE + CODEX SignalStrips), all /api/* 200. Full gates green: tsc, eslint, prettier, vitest 1743/1743.

title: Rework navigation around distinct context models
description:
Redesign the web left navigation and context handling so the top Folder + Agent context applies only to Configure and Library. Workspace is an aggregate instance-management/inventory area; Runtime is machine-wide activity/history; Operate is explicitly target-bound. Preserve the five top-level areas while making scope and target selection visible and preventing hidden context leakage between modes. This epic records the agreed navigation strategy and sequences the implementation beads below.

Scope contract:
- Configure + Library share selected instance × selected agent context.
- Workspace defaults to aggregate across instances; page-local filters and explicit Configure links select a target.
- Runtime defaults to machine-wide activity/history; filters are local to Runtime pages.
- Operate requires an explicit instance/repository target per operational surface.
- Cross-area links carry explicit instance/agent targets where needed.
- The top context chooser is mode-aware and is not presented as a global control.

References: docs/DESIGN.md §4-§5; docs/SPEC.md §4.2, §5 rows 1-24; docs/USAGE.md Feature areas and navigation.
design: Use the existing five rail groups as the stable top-level information architecture. Separate configuration context from aggregate and operational targeting. Treat scope as part of navigation state, not an implicit global side effect. Keep target selection explicit at the point of action for Git, Terminal, and Pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: A documented and tested navigation contract exists; Configure/Library context is isolated from Workspace/Runtime/Operate state; aggregate and operational targets are explicit; route links preserve intended targets; shell and page-level UI reflect the contract; relevant tests and docs are updated.

Keep the per-row agent link for the also-applies affordance.

title: T6 Canary secret leak sweep across every output surface
description: WHAT THE LAYER DOES: verifies no secret from scanned config reaches ANY output surface — report JSON, WS payloads, HTTP responses, logs, diff previews, search snippets. This is the product core promise: it reads files full of API keys by design. WHAT MAKES A GOOD ONE: enumerates surfaces mechanically instead of testing surfaces someone remembered — plant a distinctive canary secret in a fixture tree, boot the real server, then sweep EVERY endpoint / WS payload / log file for the canary string so new endpoints get covered automatically; treats truncation and boundaries as first-class cases (search-snippet boundary fragment 7yb.7, partial .env values); asserts against the WIRE format, not the in-memory object — serialization is where past leaks happened (fix.patch np8.7, CLI disk log gxo.1). CURRENT STATE: redaction unit tests solid, but no cross-surface canary sweep; known open leak-class bugs 0p5 (opencode extras.providers verbatim) and 7yb.7 (snippet redacts truncated text) — the sweep should be built to CATCH both, then they get fixed until it passes. WORK: fixture tree with canaries per secret class, sweep script iterating all routes (walk the Hono route table if feasible) + WS + logs, wire into npm test or e2e.

title: T3 Checked-in CDP real-browser e2e against the built bundle
description: WHAT THE LAYER DOES: launches the real built server + dist/web bundle in headless Chrome driven over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. The only layer that catches browser-only failure classes — the fetch Illegal-invocation bug (agentconfig-4a3) shipped a completely dead UI while all unit tests, curl, and CLI stayed green. WHAT MAKES A GOOD ONE: runs the real artifact (built bundle, tokenized launch URL), never the dev server; asserts evidence a human would trust — Network.requestWillBeSent shows /api requests actually fired, rendered text present, any console error is a hard failure; a few deep journeys over many shallow ones: boot to dashboard with data, Hooks page shows global rows with source badge, one write flow through diff-preview to commit, one global write surfaces the ALL-PROJECTS warning; fast and boring enough for CI on every PR. CURRENT STATE: GAP — technique proven in scratchpad cdp.mjs / shot.mjs scripts (used to verify 4a3 and E12 pixels) but nothing checked in or repeatable. WORK: scripts/e2e-browser.mjs (or similar) + npm run e2e:browser, reusing the scratchpad CDP pattern; document the headless Chrome dependency.

title: Define provider/extension capability matrix
description: Inventory the extension/plugin concepts for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Continue, Copilot, Gemini CLI, Aider, and opencode; record authoritative source (CLI/config dir/manifest), scope semantics, list/detail/install/remove capabilities, version/source fields, and safety/availability behavior. Decide which non-Claude provider is first after Claude based on detectable local state and maintenance cost.
notes:
Provider/extension capability matrix (2026-08-01)

Scope and evidence
- Repository evidence: src/core/detectors/*.ts, src/core/runtimes/table.ts, src/core/scanner.ts, src/server/marketplace.ts, src/server/catalog.ts, README.md, fixtures/README.md. The app currently auto-detects all eight requested runtimes and scans project/global config dirs via KNOWN_DIRS; only Claude has a provider-specific marketplace route.
- Upstream sources checked: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference; https://geminicli.com/docs/extensions/reference/ and https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/cli-reference/; https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/customize-copilot/customize-cloud-agent/add-skills and https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-sdk/features/plugin-directories; https://docs.continue.dev/reference and https://docs.continue.dev/cli/configuration; https://dev.opencode.ai/docs/plugins/. These are vendor/maintainer documentation, not third-party summaries.
- Capability meanings: “observe” means discover/read local state; “delegate” means invoke the provider CLI/API rather than reimplementing its installer; “native extension” means the provider has a current, provider-owned package/manifest/install lifecycle. “—” is intentionally unsupported/not a provider concept, not an assumed negative.

Matrix
| Provider | Native extension concept + authoritative source | Local detection / scope semantics | List/detail/install/remove | Version/source fields | Safety / availability |
| Claude Code | Plugins bundle skills, agents, hooks, MCP/LSP/monitors; optional .claude-plugin/plugin.json. CLI: claude plugin list [--json|--available], plugin details, install/update/uninstall; marketplace catalogs. | Existing detector: CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings*.json, .claude/{agents,skills,commands,...}; project .claude; global ~/.claude. Plugin scopes user ~/.claude/settings.json, project .claude/settings.json, local .claude/settings.local.json, managed read-only. | Native + already implemented via delegated claude subprocess: marketplace list/available, installed list, install; app catalog has its own direct-write install/remove. Detail/update/enable/disable/uninstall/marketplace management remain missing in app. | Official list exposes version, source marketplace, enable status; app parses id/name/version/scope/installedAt/source/marketplace/installCount. | CLI absent/timeout/malformed output degrades to typed unavailable. Plugins are arbitrary-code/high-trust; keep subprocess fixed-argv, allowlist, timeout, redaction, and never direct-write Claude plugin state.
| Codex | No provider marketplace/plugin manager established in current repository/docs. Native customization is layered AGENTS.md plus ~/.codex/config.toml and MCP config; model/tool config, not an installable extension package. | Existing detector: AGENTS.md, .codex/config.toml/rules; project AGENTS.md/.codex; global ~/.codex; scanner prunes sessions/app state. AGENTS.md is shared and can false-positive with other runtimes. | Observe local files and normalized artifacts only. No provider CLI list/detail/install/remove contract; do not invent one. Agentconfig Catalog may install inert skills/agents/MCP/config files through its own provenance path, but label that agentconfig-managed, not Codex-managed. | Config has model/profile/MCP identifiers; no canonical extension id/version/source/installedAt. Preserve file path + sha256 + parser metadata instead. | Highest local detectability/lowest maintenance: existing detector, scanner, global store, write guards, and shared AGENTS.md. Availability is filesystem-based; do not require codex CLI.
| Cursor | Editor extension marketplace is separate from Cursor AI rules. Provider-owned project customization is .cursor/rules/*.mdc plus deprecated .cursorrules; user rules live in app settings. No stable Cursor CLI plugin-manager contract found in repository scope. | Existing detector: .cursor/ and .cursorrules; project only in current scanner, global rule state is not file-addressable. | Observe rules/config only. VS Code/Cursor editor extensions are out of scope for agentconfig unless a separate editor marketplace adapter is designed; no safe provider install/remove. | Rule frontmatter has description/globs/alwaysApply; no extension package version/source in project files. | Rules are inert-ish prompt/config data but may contain injection; render as text and apply existing redaction. Availability should be “detected rules”, not “Cursor plugin manager unavailable.”
| Continue | Continue config is an agent composition of models, rules, prompts/context/tools/MCP; official config.yaml reference and ~/.continue/config.yaml. Not a single provider plugin package lifecycle. | Existing detector: .continue/config.json|yaml|yml, .continue/ files, legacy .continuerules; project and global ~/.continue supported by detector/scanner. | Observe config/rules/models/tools. No canonical provider list/detail/install/remove command in current docs; hub references/config selection are not a general extension installer. | Model/provider/model names, config name/version/schema where present; no canonical installed extension source/version. | Config format has churn/legacy JSON+YAML; parser should be defensive and expose format confidence. Avoid writes beyond known config/rules paths.
| Copilot | Current GitHub Copilot supports agent skills (SKILL.md), custom agents, hooks, MCP, and SDK plugin directories; official docs describe .github/skills, .github/agents, .github/hooks, and ~/.copilot/skills. This is a host/surface-dependent customization model, not one universal marketplace for all Copilot surfaces. | Existing detector covers .github/copilot-instructions.md and .github/copilot plus path-scoped .github/instructions/*.instructions.md; scanner should expand only with explicit support for .github/skills, .github/agents, .github/hooks and ~/.copilot. | Observe skill/agent/hook/MCP files. GitHub CLI gh skill can search/preview/install/update, but is public preview and may target multiple hosts; do not make it a required provider adapter in v1. No general Copilot remove/detail contract chosen. | gh skill provenance can include repo/ref/tree SHA in SKILL.md frontmatter; custom-agent files have frontmatter but no universal package version. | Skills are unverified and may contain prompt injections/scripts per GitHub docs; preview/read-only first, never silently install. CLI/API availability and plan/surface vary.
| Gemini CLI | First-class extensions with gemini-extension.json; packages MCP servers, context, commands, hooks, sub-agents, skills, themes. CLI: gemini extensions list/install/uninstall/enable/disable/update/link/new/validate. | Existing detector: GEMINI.md/.gemini; global ~/.gemini. Extension home is ~/.gemini/extensions/<name>; workspace disable scope exists per official docs. Project extension state is not currently in scanner allowlist. | Native CLI provides full lifecycle; agentconfig should delegate fixed argv and parse bounded JSON/text, or initially read install metadata only. No direct writes to ~/.gemini/extensions. | Manifest name/version/description; install metadata .gemini-extension-install.json has source/type; install supports Git/local source and --ref/auto-update/pre-release. | Strong candidate but more implementation surface than Codex: Git/source fetching, copied installs, symlink link mode, user/workspace enablement, settings/keychain, arbitrary MCP/hooks/scripts. CLI absent should be unavailable, not an error.
| Aider | No native plugin/marketplace package lifecycle identified. Configuration is .aider.conf.yml, .aiderignore, conventions passed via --read/read entries, plus CLI options. | Existing detector: .aider.conf.yml/.aiderignore; project files only; no canonical Aider global extension directory in current source table. | Observe config/read files; no provider list/detail/install/remove. Agentconfig Catalog can manage inert config artifacts separately. | YAML config has model/read/lint/test settings; no extension identity/version/source. | Low risk to observe; do not claim plugin support or execute arbitrary read/lint/test commands from config.
| opencode | Native plugins are JS/TS modules loaded from global ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ and project .opencode/plugins/; official plugin docs define plugin hooks/API, but current docs do not establish a stable marketplace/install/remove command contract. | Existing detector: opencode.json/.opencode; project and global ~/.config/opencode represented in runtime table; plugin path is not yet a first-class scanner artifact. | Observe plugin files/config only in v1. No provider install/remove until CLI contract and manifest/version semantics stabilize; do not npm-install or execute plugin code. | opencode.json has model/provider/agent/MCP fields; plugin package metadata may be package.json, but no canonical provider inventory contract selected. | High execution risk: plugins are code and may pull dependencies; CLI/documentation is moving quickly. Defer provider-managed mutation and expose “code plugins present; management unavailable.”
 
Decision
Recommended first non-Claude provider: Codex, for a normalized read-only extension/config provider, not a native install adapter. It wins on detectable local state and maintenance cost: detector + fixture + global scan already exist; AGENTS.md and ~/.codex/config.toml are stable filesystem inputs; scanner/pathguard/global-store/security behavior is already exercised; no provider-specific marketplace, network, package execution, or version-resolution lifecycle must be cloned. The first contract can expose provider=codex, scope project/global, artifact kind instruction/config/MCP/rule, path, sha256, parsed metadata, source=local, and capabilities {observe:true, list:true, detail:true, install:false, remove:false, update:false}. Keep Claude as the only delegated native marketplace adapter. Gemini CLI is the recommended second non-Claude adapter after the read-only contract because it has the clearest full extension lifecycle, but it must be isolated behind CLI delegation and stronger trust/availability handling.

Implementation boundary for the next bead
- Normalize capabilities per provider instead of forcing every runtime into plugin semantics: extension model (native|config|rules|none), scopes, artifacts, list/detail/install/remove/update/enable/disable, source/version support, availability state, and trust level.
- Required UI/API states: supported, detected, unavailable (CLI missing), unsupported, and error; do not collapse unsupported into unavailable.
- Never execute or direct-write provider plugin code/state. Native lifecycle adapters must use fixed argv, timeouts, bounded output, defensive parsing, and provider-owned uninstall. Agentconfig Catalog remains separately provenance-tracked and diff-previewed.
- Matrix status: complete for planning; no application code changed; keep this bead open only if product owner wants a different first provider.
close_reason: Capability matrix recorded in bead notes; Codex selected as first non-Claude read-only provider, Gemini CLI as second native lifecycle candidate; no application code changed.
